To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the alpha-relaxation of pDCPD is dominated by intra-chain motions, and that sub-Tg relaxaiton is dominated by localized motions.

the glass transition of pDCPD is dominated by the dynamics of individual polymer chains and the dynamics of the network is controlled by molecular motions that occur on the length scale of individual chains.

the alpha-relaxation of cross-linked pDCPD networks is linked to intra- and inter-chain segmental motions and large-scale chain motions, while sub-glass transitions are dominated by more localized chain motions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the glass transition and the molecular motions that underlie this transition in pDCPD networks.
the glassy state of pDCPD, and how the glassy state is related to the structure of the polymer chains.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that control the glass transition and mechanical properties in pDCPD networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the glass transition of a pDCPD network is a complex process that is controlled by a variety of molecular mechanisms.
the glass transition in pDCPD networks is controlled by a combination of local, intermediate and global motions.
pDCPD networks exhibit a strong dependence of the glass transition on molecular weight between crosslinks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the glass transition of pDCPD is a result of a competition of intra-chain and large-scale motions, with the relative importance of the two types of motions dependent upon molecular weight between cross-link points.
the alpha-relaxation is controlled by the interplay between the intra- and sub-Tg motions, and the latter is controlled by the molecular weight between crosslinks.
cross-linking has a profound impact on the molecular motions of the pDCPD networks and these motions control their mechanical and transport properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular weight between crosslinks is a critical parameter that controls the mechanical and transport properties of the polymer network.
pDCPD networks are unique among cross-linked networks in the degree of coupling between the alpha-relaxation and the sub-Tg relaxational processes.
the glass transition of pDCPD is controlled by the balance between inter- and intra-chain interactions, and that the inter-chain interactions control the strength of the alpha-relaxation.
